summary: Well‑executed preregistered paired study that transparently archives artifacts and correctly treats the exact two‑sided McNemar as the preregistered primary inferential outcome. The manuscript carefully documents shared_initial_candidate semantics, model/config provenance (including temperature=null caveat), execution accounting, deterministic validator behavior, and limitations stemming from very high baseline validity and sparse repairs. Key issues to resolve in the paper are limited and resolvable from the archived artifacts (preregistration and bibliography).
critical_issues: The manuscript reports a preregistered‑adjacent one‑sided McNemar sensitivity (p=0.03125) but the provided preregistration text and multiplicity plan do not explicitly enumerate a one‑sided McNemar as a preregistered confirmatory or sensitivity test. The paper must clearly state whether the one‑sided test was explicitly preregistered (and point to the exact preregistration location) or else label it as post‑hoc. This is a material preregistration‑fidelity disclosure.

The References/citation metadata as presented in the run evidence bundle include DOI/arXiv/OpenAlex identifiers; the manuscript must present a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography (full bibliographic metadata: authors, title, venue, year) and ensure that each numbered citation in the prose corresponds to a verified record that supports the proximate scholarly claim. Replace bare identifier entries with full IEEE‑style entries using the verified bibliography record.

The manuscript presents a paired confirmatory design whose power justification assumed baseline≈0.60 and target effect≈0.15 in the preregistration, but the observed baseline success rate (0.995) is far higher than the preregistered assumption. Although limitations mention low baseline failure prevalence, the paper must more explicitly reconcile the preregistered power assumptions with the observed data (i.e., state the mismatch and its consequences for inferential sensitivity).
required_revisions: In Methods/Preregistration section explicitly state whether the one‑sided exact McNemar sensitivity was prespecified in the archived preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001); if prespecified, provide the exact preregistration excerpt or pointer (artifact path/manifest entry) where it appears; if not prespecified, label the one‑sided result as post‑hoc and soften any claims accordingly. This must be resolved using the supplied preregistration artifact.

Replace/augment the current References list with a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/arXiv) for every cited work. Ensure each in‑text numeric citation refers to a verified record and that the prose citations (e.g., claims about hallucination, constrained decoding, verifier‑assisted repair) are supported by the cited record(s). Use the supplied verified bibliography/search artifacts to build the IEEE entries; do not invent metadata.

In Methods or Limitations explicitly reconcile the preregistered power/precision assumptions with the observed baseline success rate (0.995). State that the preregistered target effect and power calculation assumed a much higher baseline failure prevalence, describe how that mismatch reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains, and confirm that no additional confirmatory inference beyond the preregistered McNemar was carried out. This clarification should be drawn from the archived power_and_precision_plan and execution artifacts.
optional_revisions: Consider adding a brief, explicit sentence in Methods pointing to execution/model_configuration.json and stating temperature=null was recorded and does not imply deterministic sampling (the manuscript already notes this—merely consider placing it adjacent to the model configuration citation for clarity).

Add a short table or text snippet (can be a one‑paragraph insert) summarizing the preregistered analysis flow (primary vs secondary vs sensitivity) with exact artifact paths to the preregistration and analysis_log.jsonl to make it trivial for readers/reviewers to verify claim–artifact links.

In Discussion, expand (briefly) on recommended follow‑ups quantifying how varying repair budget, validator coverage, or independent (non‑shared) initial generations would change the estimand and detectable effect sizes; cite specific archived artifacts (e.g., deterministic_reconciliation.json) when motivating suggested experiment variants.
